note: 'And he conferred with Joab ... and with Abiathar the priest' (1Kgs 1:7); Abiathar is at the feast at 1:25 and loses the priesthood for it.

'Let King Solomon first swear to me not to put his servant to the sword.' (1Kgs 1:51), said with both hands on the horns of the altar. Solomon answers with a condition rather than an oath (1:52), and collects on it in the next chapter.
'I will be king!” And he acquired chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him.' (1Kgs 1:5) -- while his father lived and, as Nathan puts it, 'our lord David does not know it' (1:11).

'And Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen, and fattened calves near the stone of Zoheleth, which is next to En-rogel.' (1Kgs 1:9) -- the rival feast, close enough to Gihon that his guests hear the trumpet (1:41).
'My lord,” she replied, “you yourself swore to your maidservant by the LORD your God: Surely your son Solomon will reign after me' (1Kgs 1:17). She holds him to an oath the reader has not been shown.
'Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon' (1Kgs 1:45), as David directed at 1:34.
held: inside quoted speech (the Berean's quotation marks), speaker not on record

note: 'My lord the king,” said Nathan, “did you say, Adonijah will reign after me' (1Kgs 1:24) -- arriving on cue, exactly as he arranged with Bathsheba at 1:14.

'Then Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king' (1Kgs 1:11), and tells her why it matters: 'Save your own life and the life of your son Solomon' (1:12).
Brought down on David's own mule, escorted by the Cherethites and the Pelethites (1Kgs 1:38).
'Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Solomon.' (1Kgs 1:39).
